headline: Local Kirana Store Owner Declares Trade War On Neighborhood Auntie Over Unreciprocated Dahi-Vada Exchange
body:
Ramesh Kumar, proprietor of 'Sudarshan General Store', has officially frozen all supply lines of premium salted peanuts to Mrs. Sharma, a regular customer, citing a total failure of reciprocity in their neighborhood food-swapping arrangement. The trade dispute, which escalated early Tuesday morning, hinges on the fact that while Kumar has provided three consecutive weeks of high-grade condiments, Mrs. Sharma has failed to provide a corresponding exchange of her signature dahi-vada.

“This isn’t just about the yogurt snacks; it’s about the integrity of our local supply chain,” said Kumar, while placing a cardboard blockade around the peanut display. “I am hereby authorizing a total ban on all snack-based exports to her kitchen until she restores the full reciprocity of the dahi-vada agreement. My inventory is not a charity for those who harvest my salted peanuts while offering only empty promises of tangy, curd-soaked relief in return.”

Mrs. Sharma, reached for comment while carrying a suspiciously empty plate, maintained that the trade imbalance was due to a temporary shortage of quality chickpeas and not a malicious withdrawal from their mutual cooperation pact. “Mr. Kumar is being unnecessarily protectionist,” she noted. “If he continues to restrict access to the peanuts, I will be forced to impose retaliatory tariffs on his supply of fresh coriander by sourcing it exclusively from the vendor on the next street over.”

As of press time, other shopkeepers on the lane were attempting to mediate the crisis, fearing that a full-scale trade war could lead to a collapse in local biscuit-to-tea-cookie barter ratios before the end of the week.
caption: A neighborhood trade dispute reaches a boiling point over the critical lack of dahi-vada reciprocity. Will the salted peanuts ever return to the shelves? #TradeWar #NeighborhoodDrama #KiranaLife #DahiVadaDiplomacy (satire)

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 12 stands out for its human-scale absurdity. By framing a neighborhood dispute over a 'dahi-vada' exchange as a high-stakes 'trade war' with formal blockades, it perfectly captures the specific, petty, yet warm dynamics of a community, avoiding the dry 'AI-slop' feel of the international tariff variants.
